title: Fernández-Díaz 2011 · Acoustic cue and haptic matching
citation: Fernández-Díaz and Travieso (2011). Performance in haptic geometrical matching tasks depends on movement and position of the arms. Acta Psychologica, 136(3), 382–389.
notes: Published study settings are available for inspection. See the source-backed method and remaining execution requirements.

published_method.coordinate_frame: Lateral relative to table midline and depth from near edge, in cm.
published_method.bar_setup: 20 cm pivoted bar with 1.1 cm diameter and arrow-shaped ends on a magnetized steel table.
published_method.procedure: Match test bar to reference while a 5 s sound aligns with the reference axis or correct test axis. Lift both hands at sound offset.
published_method.geometry: Reference orientation is vertical or a side-specific oblique. Bar positions include ipsilateral and both contralateral positions. The 24 nominal cells per group do not establish realized trial sequences.
published_method.routing_gap: Printed coordinates imply no collinear speaker for eight opposite-side oblique test cells if orientation follows the reference side. Actual cue choices for those cells require the source schedule.
published_method.outcome: Signed angular error against parallelity, with matched haptic comparator data reused from Experiment 1.

stimulus_type.source: Fernández-Díaz and Travieso 2011, final Acta Psychologica issue, pp. 385–386, §4.1 and Fig. 1
stimulus_type.gap: The acoustic stimulus lasts 5 s. The source describes the same speaker setup and does not restate waveform generation.

value.scope: White noise, level, brand and height are explicit for Experiment 2. Experiment 3 refers to the same setup and states its 5 s duration.
value.alignment: Vertical alignments use ipsilateral speakers. Oblique alignments use midline speakers, 45° on left bars and 135° on right bars. The issue omits a complete routing table by condition and trial.

auditory_conditions.gap: The reported layout fixes vertical and side-specific oblique bearings. The nominal test-oriented design has eight opposite-side oblique cells without a collinear speaker when the oblique angle follows the reference side.

implementation_gaps: Requires the physical bar apparatus, continuous angular capture and four separately routed speakers.
Missing realized trial list, group assignment and exact speaker routing prevent reconstruction of all trial cells.
